# Introduction

[MetaboLights](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/) deposits every study as a
set of ISA-TAB files: an *investigation* file with the study-level metadata,
a *sample* file, one *assay* file per analytical assay linking samples to
data files, and one *metabolite assignment file* (MAF) per assay with the
reported metabolites and their abundances per sample. The
`r Biocpkg("MsBackendMetaboLights")` package [@Rainer2024] gives access to
these files and to the raw MS data.

`r Biocpkg("mtbls2mztabm")` builds on it and turns the ISA-TAB files
of a study into two things Bioconductor and the wider metabolomics community
can work with directly:

- a `SummarizedExperiment` [@Morgan] holding the MAF abundances with the
  sample and feature annotations, laid out like the object produced by the
  `r Biocpkg("xcms")` preprocessing workflow for MetaboLights data so that
  both can be handled by the same downstream code;
- an [mzTab-M 2.1](https://github.com/HUPO-PSI/mzTab-M) file
  [@Hoffmann2019], written with the *RmzTabM* package, whose metadata section
  is filled from the investigation and assay tables.

The study used throughout is
[MTBLS103](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/MTBLS103), an NMR and LC-MS
metabolomics study of serum from adolescents with hyperinsulinaemic androgen
excess [@Samino2015]. Its ISA-TAB files are also shipped with the package, so
every step below can be reproduced without network access by adding
`path = system.file("extdata", "MTBLS103", package = "mtbls2mztabm")`
to the calls. A second study of a different kind, the GC-MS study MTBLS40,
is exported in the same way towards the end.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("mtbls2mztabm")
```

```{r load}
library(mtbls2mztabm)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# The study and its factors

The investigation file is returned as a named list of records.

```{r investigation}
inv <- mtbls_investigation("MTBLS103")
inv[["Study Title"]]
inv[["Study Assay File Name"]]
```

MTBLS103 has one experimental factor, *HIAE*, with the levels `CTR`
(healthy controls), `HIAE` (patients at diagnosis) and `TREAT` (the same
patients after 18 months of treatment).

```{r factors}
mtbls_factors("MTBLS103")
fv <- mtbls_factor_values("MTBLS103")
table(fv$hiae)
```

# A SummarizedExperiment of one assay

Of the four assays, the HILIC LC-MS assay is used here. The abundance matrix
of its MAF becomes the assay data, the ISA-TAB sample and assay tables the
`colData()` and the MAF annotations the `rowData()`.

```{r se}
se <- mtbls_summarized_experiment(
    "MTBLS103",
    assayName = "a_MTBLS103_ibanez_02_HILIC_mass_spectrometry.txt")
se
```

The `colData()` follows the layout of the xcms MetaboLights workflow. The
`species` and `tissue` columns are mzTab-M controlled-vocabulary parameters
built from the ontology terms of the sample file; fields the study does not
deposit, such as the age of the participants, are `NA`.

```{r coldata}
colData(se)[1:4, c("sample_name", "phenotype", "species", "tissue",
                   "polarity")]
```

The MAF of MTBLS103 reports 13 identified metabolites but no m/z or
retention time, so `mzmed` and `rtmed` are `NA` here; the count columns give
the number of samples with a reported abundance per phenotype level.

```{r rowdata}
rowData(se)[, c("feature_id", "npeaks", "CTR", "HIAE", "TREAT",
                "database_identifier", "metabolite_identification")]
```

```{r assay}
assay(se, "raw")[1:5, 1:3]
```

# Export to mzTab-M

`mtbls_to_mztabm()` does all of the above and writes the mzTab-M file in one
call. With several assays and no `assayName` the first mass spectrometry
assay is chosen and named in the message.

```{r export}
out <- mtbls_to_mztabm(
    "MTBLS103", file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103.mztab"),
    assayName = "a_MTBLS103_ibanez_02_HILIC_mass_spectrometry.txt")
```

The file starts with the metadata section. Instrument, ion source and mass
analyzer come from the assay table, title, description and publication from
the investigation, and the compound database from the ChEBI identifiers of
the MAF.

```{r mztab-head}
lns <- readLines(out)
lns[grepl("^MTD\t(mzTab-ID|title|publication|instrument|database\\[1\\])",
          lns)]
```

Every sample, MS run and assay of the study is listed, followed by the
small molecule feature table with one row per metabolite.

```{r mztab-counts}
c(MTD = sum(startsWith(lns, "MTD\t")),
  SMF = sum(startsWith(lns, "SMF\t")))
RmzTabM::readMzTabM(out)
```

The `SummarizedExperiment` and the `MzTabM` object are attached to the
returned path for further work in R.

```{r attrs}
attr(out, "mztabm")
```

# A GC-MS study: MTBLS40

The same call serves any MetaboLights study with a mass spectrometry assay.
[MTBLS40](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/MTBLS40) is a GC-TOF-MS study
of *Arabidopsis thaliana* wild type and two mutants (`Col-0`, `mto1` and
`tt4`) [@Kusano2007]. Its assay table lists the raw netCDF data files only,
so these become the `ms_run`s of the mzTab-M file, the factor *Genotype*
becomes the study variables and the MAF contributes 171 features with
retention times and, where identified, ChEBI identifiers.

```{r mtbls40}
out40 <- mtbls_to_mztabm("MTBLS40",
                         file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS40.mztab"))
lns40 <- readLines(out40)
lns40[grepl("^MTD\t(ms_run\\[1\\]|instrument|study_variable\\[[1-4]\\]\t)",
            lns40)]
```

```{r mtbls40-se}
se40 <- attr(out40, "se")
table(se40$phenotype)
head(rowData(se40)[, c("feature_id", "rtmed", "database_identifier",
                       "metabolite_identification")])
```

The ISA-TAB files of MTBLS40 are shipped with the package as well, under
`system.file("extdata", "MTBLS40", package = "mtbls2mztabm")`.

# What the ISA-TAB files cannot provide

A MAF is a table of reported abundances, not a processing result: it has no
gap-filled counterpart, so `raw_filled` equals `raw`; peak ranges (`mzmin`,
`mzmax`, `rtmin`, `rtmax`) are always `NA`; and `injection_index` is the row
order of the assay table, not a verified acquisition order. mzTab-M contacts
require an ORCID, which ISA-TAB investigation files rarely carry, so the
contact section is left out unless one is present.
